# v2.5.7 "Collimation"

**Sprite rendering closes exact — the phase was wrong by two dots, and every window was compensating.**

Collimation is the act of bringing two optical axes true. Until it is done, two sightlines can agree and both be wrong — and that is literally what this release found.

## The finding

The boot traces agreed on `scanline`/`dot` at every instruction boundary, all 36,392 records, which read as "no phase offset." The per-cycle traces said otherwise: the DUT's cycle 103973 covered PPU dots 245–247 against the oracle's 247–249.

Both were true. A two-dot CPU–PPU power-on phase error was hidden by an equal record-point offset in the testbench — two errors cancelling exactly. The earlier `PPU_LEAD` sweep had tested 0 and 3; the answer, **2**, sat between them, never tried until the two mappings were reconciled by hand. Unlike 3, a two-dot shift preserves dot parity, which is why 2 composes where 3 needed an epicycle.

`PPU_LEAD=2` alone closed `ppuspr020` exactly and broke three other gates — the signature of compensations fitted at the wrong phase. The coherent set:

- Every OAM window moves from documented-minus-three to **documented-minus-one** — and minus-one is registered-assignment semantics (a write at dot D is visible at D+1), not an offset. Presentation lands on the documented dots exactly, with no residual fudge. The RTL's own comment block had claimed "MINUS ONE" all along, while the code sat at minus-three. **The phase fix brought the code to the prose.**
- The rendering-enable delay shrinks 3 dots → 1: the `$2001` write lands two dots later in the stream, so the write-to-effect distance is unchanged and the fetch gate holds without retuning.
- The boot record samples at the top of the cycle, removing the cancellation's other half — so the phase gate now passes with the true phase rather than with two errors summing to zero.

## Every gate exact

First time in the rung with zero divergences anywhere:

| gate | result |
| --- | --- |
| `ppuspr019` / `ppuspr020` / `ppuspr021` | 119,115 cycles each |
| `ppuscroll` / `ppusprender` / `ppusprite` | 49,998 / 119,114 / 59,993 |
| `ppuregs` | 12,841 records |
| background / sprite fetch traces | 7,058 / 88,685 |
| all three index framebuffers | 61,440 pixels each |
| `nestest` | 59,554 cycles |
| `ppu-phase-gate` (new) | 98,562 records |

## What lands

**Sprite rendering, priority, sprite-0 hit, overflow** — eight slots, the priority mux, the left-8 masks, the no-hit-at-x=255 quirk, garbage nametable fetches, the 337/339 dummies — gated across four declared surfaces plus three purpose-built sprite-0 edge ROMs (`ppuspr019/020/021`: transparent background, X=248 boundary, X=255).

**The odd-frame skipped dot.** Its absence was a *drift*, not an offset — `ppuspr020`'s first frame agreed exactly and its second was one read late, because the DUT never skipped pre-render dot 339 on odd rendering frames. The gate that can see a one-dot-per-odd-frame drift is new: **`ppu-phase-gate`**, the inverse of `cpu-gate`'s skip list — `scanline` and `dot` are the *only* fields compared, over twelve frames so the skip fires about six times.

**`cpu_ce` — the register file was gated by nothing.** `PPU_SUBDOT`, a master-clock-resolution instrument built to test whether the half-dot between `read_split` and `write_split` is observable (it is not — now measured rather than argued), found instead that every `$2000`–`$2007` write latched on *every* clock edge, correct only because the harness pulsed the decode once per cycle. Latent until v2.6.5, where `nes_top` holds a decoded address for the full 12-master-clock cycle and every write would latch twelve times. Fixed with a one-clock commit strobe separate from the decode; the pre-fix behaviour is CAUGHT by two independent gates.

## The mutation catalog, all ten CAUGHT

Re-run in full at the corrected phase, because a phase change is more invasive than a stimulus change. The tenth — sprite-0 flag read from the register only — is caught by `ppuspr020` at **exactly one divergence: the read landing on the hit dot**. The `$2004` readback-off-by-one mutant reproduced the old catalog's exact count, 110.

Classified non-gaps, each with evidence and an owner:

| mutation | classification |
| --- | --- |
| vblank read from register only | stimulus gap on the v2.5.8 race dot — a stimulus built now would pin pre-race semantics v2.5.8 rewrites |
| skip-check delay collapsed | needs a `$2001` toggle across dot 339 — blargg `10-even_odd_timing`, needs v2.5.8's VBlank sync |
| `chr_wr` reverted to decode-only | out of stimulus, **measured**: 0 assertions across all eight CHR-ROM ROMs; reachable at v2.6.3 |
| sprite fetch slot uniformly +1 | inert — source and destination indices shift together; final state byte-identical |
| `cpu_cs` reverted to the `cs && ce` product | inert — idempotent AND |

The re-run also caught its own harness twice: a pattern carrying a literal `\n` matched nothing and silently reported the *baseline* as NOT CAUGHT, and a three-occurrence pattern would have mutated the wrong site. The harness now refuses a verdict unless a pattern applies exactly once.

## The oracle side

**Zero emulation-core changes** — the diff is one diagnostic printout in the test harness (`status` beside `oam_bus` in the sprite-eval probe) — so **AccuracyCoin holds 141/141 (100.00%, RAM decoder)** and nestest stays 0-diff by construction.
